SMTO-GWT-0023 — The Gateway computer changed before SMTO's next step

GUID: fc7ba766-773d-4d3a-bc2e-5d3a220da544
Slug: gateway-profile-changed
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • While SMTO was deciding what to do next, the setup on the Gateway computer changed, for example after an update or restart. SMTO didn't run that step and needs to choose it again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for the Gateway this Task uses. This loads the Gateway's current setup so SMTO plans with the right information.
  2. Make sure it is still the computer you meant to use, and that nobody is updating or reconfiguring it right now. SMTO stops here when the Gateway's setup changes between planning and running a step.
  3. In the conversation, ask SMTO to continue the Task, or send your request again. The step was not run, so SMTO can safely choose it again with the new setup.

What success looks like

  • The Task continues and its next step runs on the Gateway without this message.

If it still fails

  • If the message keeps coming back, the Gateway may be restarting over and over. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't point an older saved Task at a different Gateway; start a new Task instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway preflight found the target's execution profile (platform, shell or capability snapshot) changed since the plan was made, or a resumed run's capability snapshot names a different Gateway than the saved target, so dispatch was refused and a new plan is required.

What this means

  • The Gateway capability snapshot no longer matches the captured target, or pre-dispatch checks detected a changed environment profile and require a new plan. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The Gateway capability snapshot no longer matches the captured target, or pre-dispatch checks detected a changed environment profile and require a new plan.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the planned snapshot with the current target identity and capabilities; keep identity-change failures distinct from capability changes.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the Gateway record's current execution profile (platform, shell, capability tags) against the run's saved profile; changes usually follow a Gateway update, restart or reconfiguration. Refresh the Gateway with Check connection, then let the agent replan (the tool result carries replan_required=true and executed=false); a resumed run that names a different Gateway than its saved target must be started as a new Task rather than retargeted.
  • Refresh the selected Gateway profile and confirm the intended environment before continuing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The next authorized decision uses the refreshed profile of the same verified target.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
